To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ultrasound assisted reaction of 2-acetoxy-3,4,5,6-tetramethoxybenzyl bromide with curcumin in the presence of phase transfer catalyst in aqueous media results in high yield of mono- and di-beta-glucopyranose derivatives of curcmin.

the reaction of 2-acetoxy-3,4,5,6-tetramethylbenzenesulfonic acid with 2,3-epoxypropyl alcohol in a mixture of 1,4-dioxane and acetonitrile in the presence of 18-crown-6 and tetrabutylammonium bromide under ultrasound irradiation gave the corresponding ether in good yields.

the glucosylation reaction of curcumin with glucose under the effect of ultrasonic waves in the presence of phase transfer catalysts is faster and results in the increased yield and selectivity of the glucosidic products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of beta-glucosides of curcumin by reacting 2,3-4,6-tetracetyl-alpha-D-glucose with potassium salt of the curcumin under phase transfer catalysis conditions.
the development of a simple synthetic protocol of curcumin glucosides using ultrasonic waves and phase transfer catalysts.
the synthesis of beta-glucosides of curcumin, which is a potential anti-cancer agent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glucosides of curcumin can be obtained in high yield and selectivity using a simple and efficient protocol under the effect of ultrasonic waves.
ultrasound-assisted reactions under phase-transfer catalytic conditions are faster, more effective and result in higher yields than the conventional methods.

the glucosides could be synthesized in good yields and selectivity by the reaction of curcumin and 2,3:4,5-di-O-isopropylidene-beta-D-ribonofuranosyl bromide in the presence of phase transfer catalyst under ultrasound irradiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of ultrasonic waves in the reaction between curcumin and 2,3-4,6-tetracetyl-alpha-D-glucose bromide under phase transfer conditions results in a drastic improvement in the yield and selectivity of the glucosidation process.
the glucoside formation is a very complex reaction which can be controlled by a variety of parameters such as nature and concentration of the catalyst and the reaction medium.

the glucosylation of curcumin with 2,3.4.6-tetra- O -acetyl-alpha-D-glucose under biphasic conditions using phase transfer catalysts under the effect of ultrasonic waves is a convenient and effective method for the preparation of glucoside derivatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ultrasound-assisted synthesis of curcumin glucoside derivatives is an efficient, ecofriendly, and green process.
the use of ultrasound as a reaction tool in the synthesis of curcumin glucosides is highly effective in increasing the yield of the products and selectivity of the mono-glucoside products.
the glucoside derivative of curcumin can be obtained in high yields and purity under the sonochemical reaction conditions.
